result.summary: The proposed detector misses the once-per-redaction regression it explicitly claims to catch.

findings.title: Seed above the cap before the first redaction
findings.body: With 49 seeded files, pruning after each redaction produces the same observed count as correct once-per-run pruning: the first call sees 50 files and returns without deleting; the second sees 51 and attempts one deletion. Executing the actual helper with simulated directory entries confirmed both schedules produce one intercepted delete, while the declared duplicate-at-end mutation produces two. Thus the RED proof can pass while the detector misses a per-redaction violation of N2.
findings.recommendation: Seed 50 files and adjust the expected delete count: correct final pruning attempts two deletes, per-redaction pruning attempts three, and duplicated final pruning attempts four. Verify both regression schedules and update the seam's cardinality claims accordingly.

next_steps: Revise the fixture and demonstrate that both duplicated final pruning and per-redaction pruning fail the detector.
